record_identity.title: Accenture–IE University African value-chain report published inaccurate citations and claims

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Accenture and IE University published the November 2025 report Leapfrogging Development; GPTZero reported citation discrepancies in November 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: The artefact was first public on 2025-11-12; 4 November 2026 is the date of external discovery and scrutiny, not a claim of continuous writing or publication up to that day. For revised papers each later version is part of the same publication occurrence.

summary: On 12 November 2025, Accenture Africa and IE University published a research and policy report on opportunities for AI in African agricultural value chains. The published PDF included inaccurate source descriptions and factual claims, including a statement that Ghana and Uganda ranked 47th and 74th in a 2023 AI readiness index; the original index reports different positions. On 4 November 2026, GPTZero published a detailed comparison identifying 15 purportedly fabricated or significantly mangled references among 89 citations and additional unsupported assertions. Accenture said its internal review attributed the errors to human error rather than AI, but announced a corrected republication; IE University said it was reviewing the evidence. The citation discrepancies and publication-stage reliance problem are observable, while whether generative AI produced specific errors, which tool was involved, and the authors' internal review sequence remain unverified.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The original Accenture-hosted PDF, page 16, contains the stated Ghana/Uganda readiness rankings. Its references on page 42 include a World Economic Forum citation with a mismatched title and publication year. GPTZero's 4 November source-by-source investigation identifies 15 of 89 report citations as fabricated or heavily distorted and separately disputes claims made using those citations. Financial Times reporting presents Accenture's denial of AI hallucination as a cause and its announced correction, with IE University's verification response. The original PDF, the source checks and correction announcement establish an observable evidence-quality and publication mismatch without requiring an internal authoring transcript.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The assessed conduct is the release and research-stage reliance on specific unfaithful citations and claims within Leapfrogging Development. The suspected participating generative-AI research/drafting component has not been identified; public output and independently checkable source discrepancies nevertheless show material below the epistemic assurance appropriate for publication. The cause remains disputed or unverified: the resulting provisional Epistemic Reliance Calibration failure applies to the observable generated/retrieved/transformed/synthesised epistemic artefact as it was supplied for scholarly or policy reliance, not an assertion that any identified LLM generated the error. The authors and publishing bodies are accountable for publication, but the available evidence does not assign the erroneous words to a specific person, model or tool. External GPTZero detection is not the assessed AI platform.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This occurrence illustrates the separation between observable deficient epistemic assurance and unknown internal generative-system topology. Professional reliance requires source verification proportionate to publication-stage evidentiary use even where model trace and authorship details are unavailable. The correction or investigator response can be recorded without transferring its actions to the assessed synthetic component.
assessment_boundaries: Accenture's investigation attributes the inaccuracies to human error and disputes GenAI causation; that account must remain visible, not overwritten by GPTZero's AI-detector score.
GPTZero's 15-of-89 count is investigator-reported; original-source checks in this review independently confirm selected mismatches, not each of the 15 items.
No specific generative AI model, prompt, drafting session or author-specific use is publicly established.
The original institutional report is the assessed publication. GPTZero's detector or review tool is external investigative evidence, not the assessed AI system.
The report was jointly issued by Accenture Africa and IE University; neither the entire Accenture organisation nor every researcher is automatically the AI operator.
An announced future correction is not evidence that a corrected publication is already online or that all affected references have been repaired.
Potential effects on agricultural policy are plausible but no adopted government decision, client loss or affected beneficiary count is evidenced.
Any FC-062 result is expressly provisional pending further source evidence of generative AI participation, not a legal or scholarly finding of deliberate deception.
Publication/author workflow uncertainty is reported as a limitation, not falsely resolved through hypothetical prompts or model selection.
No independently acting defender AI is assessed in this incident; post-publication investigations and corrections are source/outcome context.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The observable publication defect is clear: a policy/research report supplied unsupported precise statistics and questionable citations as formal evidence. Research involving generative-AI use is suspected by GPTZero's reference pattern and detector, but Accenture attributes these specific errors to human work and direct AI generation cannot be reconstructed. Provisional FC-062 is assigned to the publication-stage epistemic assurance mismatch, not to a named model's undisclosed generation step.
